agri-hdesc: Farming support from the Provincial Government of Bukidnon, and where local and national programs fit in
agri-x4: Bukidnon is known as the food basket of Mindanao. Under the Local Government Code, a province supports agricultural development across its cities and municipalities.
agri-x7: In general, this office plans and coordinates agricultural development for the province, and provides technical help and extension services to farmers.
agri-x10: Provincial agriculture programs are planned together with the Provincial Planning and Development Office and funded through the provincial budget.
agri-x13: Agriculture spending is part of the provincial budget approved by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
agri-x15: Many farm services are delivered close to the farm, so start with the office nearest you.
agri-x18: Farmers usually register and ask for local assistance at the agriculture office of their city or municipality.
agri-x20: Crop insurance, farm credit, fertilizer and seed subsidies, and registry programs come from national agencies such as the Department of Agriculture and its partners. Ask your local agriculture office which program applies.
agri-x22: Central Mindanao University in Musuan, Maramag does agricultural education and research in the province.
agri-note: This page is a general guide written by volunteers. Requirements, fees and processing times are set by each office and may vary, so confirm with the office before you go. The official source is the
biz-hdesc: Business permits are issued by your city or municipality. Here is where the Province fits in.
biz-x1: Where to get a business permit
biz-x2: In the Philippines, the mayor's permit and local business tax are handled by the city or municipality where the business is located, not by the Province.
biz-x5: Apply at the Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) of Malaybalay City, Valencia City or your municipality.
biz-x8: Read the general steps for applying and renewing a business permit.
biz-x10: Depending on the business, you may also register with the DTI (business name), the SEC or CDA, the BIR, and the barangay. Each agency sets its own requirements.
biz-x12: The Provincial Government collects certain provincial taxes and fees allowed by the Local Government Code.
biz-x15: Collects provincial taxes and fees. Ask the office whether any provincial tax applies to your kind of business.
biz-x18: The Provincial Planning and Development Office prepares the provincial development plan that guides local investment.
biz-x21: Zoning clearance and building permits are issued by the city or municipal government.
biz-note: This page is a general guide written by volunteers. Requirements, fees and processing times are set by each office and may vary, so confirm with the office before you go. The official source is the
cert-hdesc: Birth, marriage and death records are handled by your city or municipality and the PSA
cert-x2: Civil registration is done by the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) of the city or municipality where the event happened. The Province does not issue these documents.
cert-x5: Register a birth, marriage or death, or ask for a copy, at the LCRO of Malaybalay City, Valencia City or your municipality.
cert-x8: Learn how registration and PSA copies work.
cert-x11: The PSA issues the security-paper copies that many offices ask for. See psa.gov.ph for current ways to request them.
cert-x13: Each guide explains the general steps. Requirements may vary, so confirm with the civil registrar.
cert-x16: Get a copy of a birth record registered in Bukidnon.
cert-x19: Marriage registration and copies of a marriage record.
cert-x22: Death registration and copies of a death record.

edu-hdesc: The Province's role in education, and who runs schools and scholarships in Bukidnon
edu-x2: Public schools are run by the national Department of Education. Provincial and city or municipal governments support them in limited ways.
edu-x4: Under the Local Government Code, the Provincial School Board decides how the province uses its share of the Special Education Fund (SEF) for schools.
edu-x7: The Province may offer scholarships or student assistance through its programs. Ask the Provincial Governor's Office or the PSWDO for what is open now.
edu-x10: Education support is part of the provincial budget.
edu-x12: Where to go depends on the school level.
edu-x14: Enrollment, records and school concerns go to your school and the DepEd Schools Division Office of Bukidnon.
edu-x17: They also receive a share of the Special Education Fund and may run local education programs.
edu-x19: Central Mindanao University (Musuan, Maramag) and Bukidnon State University (Malaybalay City) handle their own admission and scholarships.

env-hdesc: Environmental protection in Bukidnon: provincial planning, national agencies and local governments
env-x2: The Local Government Code gives provinces a role in protecting the environment and planning land use across their territory.
env-x5: The Provincial Planning and Development Office prepares the provincial development plan, which includes the environment.
env-x8: The Office of the Provincial Agriculturist works on farm practices and related programs.
env-x11: The PDRRMD prepares the province for floods, landslides and other hazards.
env-x13: Most environmental permits and day-to-day services sit with other offices.
env-x15: Environmental clearances, tree cutting permits and protected areas such as the Mount Kitanglad Range Natural Park are handled by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.
env-x18: Collection and segregation are handled by your city, municipality and barangay.
env-x21: Provincial waterworks projects are with the Provincial Engineer's Office; local water districts and city or municipal offices run their own systems.
env-note: This page is a general guide written by volunteers. Requirements, fees and processing times are set by each office and may vary, so confirm with the office before you go. The official source is the
infra-hdesc: Provincial roads, bridges and projects, and who issues building permits
infra-x6: The Province builds and maintains provincial infrastructure under the Local Government Code.
infra-x9: In general, the PEO plans, builds and maintains provincial roads, bridges and other provincial public works.
infra-x12: The Provincial Planning and Development Office prepares the development plan that sets project priorities.
infra-x15: The Provincial General Services Office manages provincial property and procurement support.
infra-x17: Different roads and permits belong to different levels of government.
infra-x20: Building permits, occupancy permits and zoning clearances are issued by the Office of the Building Official of your city or municipality.
infra-x22: National highways and bridges are under the Department of Public Works and Highways. Barangay and municipal roads are handled by the local government concerned.
infra-x24: For a damaged provincial road or bridge, contact the Provincial Engineer's Office. For other roads, contact the city, municipality or barangay.

safety-hdesc: Emergency numbers and who responds to disasters, crime and fire in Bukidnon
safety-x10: In a life-threatening emergency, call 911 first. The other numbers are local landlines; dial (088) first if you are calling from outside the area.
safety-x13: The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department leads disaster preparedness, response and recovery in the province, working with city, municipal and barangay offices.
safety-x15: The Bukidnon Police Provincial Office (Camp Onahon, Malaybalay City) is part of the Philippine National Police. It is a national agency, not a provincial office.
safety-x17: The Bureau of Fire Protection is a national agency. The number above is for the Malaybalay City Fire Station; for other areas, ask your city or municipal fire station.
safety-x22: The Provincial Health Office can guide you to health services.
safety-x25: The PSWDO assists individuals and families in crisis situations.
safety-x28: Each city and municipality has its own disaster risk reduction office, police station and barangay officials.

social-hdesc: The Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office and local welfare offices
social-x4: Under the Local Government Code, the province provides social welfare services and supports those of its cities and municipalities.
social-x6: Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office
social-x7: The PSWDO leads provincial programs for families, children, women, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and people in crisis.
social-x9: Assistance for people in difficult situations is evaluated by social workers. Ask the PSWDO what applies to you.
social-x12: The PSWDO coordinates with city and municipal social welfare offices and barangays.
social-x14: IDs and benefits are often processed locally.
social-x16: Senior citizen, PWD and solo parent IDs
social-x17: These are usually processed at the city or municipal office for senior citizens, persons with disabilities and social welfare. Ask your city or municipal hall.
social-x19: Programs such as 4Ps are run by the Department of Social Welfare and Development, with local social welfare offices as partners.
social-x22: For emergencies call 911. For welfare concerns, call the PSWDO during office hours.

tax-hdesc: Real property tax and other payments: which treasurer to pay in Bukidnon
tax-x4: Where you pay depends on where the property is located.
tax-x7: Real property tax is handled with the Provincial Treasurer's Office. Your municipal treasurer can tell you where to pay.
tax-x10: Residents of these two cities pay the city treasurer, not the Provincial Treasurer.
tax-x13: The Provincial Assessor handles property assessment for the municipalities. Cities have their own assessors.
tax-x15: Several common payments are not collected by the Province.
tax-x18: Issued by the city or municipal treasurer.
tax-x21: Paid to the city or municipal treasurer when you get or renew your business permit.
tax-x24: Ask the Provincial Treasurer's Office about transfer tax and other provincial fees.

health-page-desc: Health services in Bukidnon are led by the Provincial Health Office. Contact the office for current programs, schedules and requirements.
health-pho-desc: The Provincial Health Office of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon is based at the Provincial Capitol Compound in Malaybalay City.
health-hours-value: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM
health-gathering: We are still gathering the list of PHO services, requirements and fees. Until then, please confirm details with the office.
